message.content: Write `/root/bench-runs/h4-daaee26c/test/app.test.mjs` (node:test + node:assert/strict, ONLY Node built-ins, ESM, Node v22) testing the existing files `/root/bench-runs/h4-daaee26c/public/app.js` and `/root/bench-runs/h4-daaee26c/public/index.html`. Do NOT modify those two files. If a test fails because app.js looks wrong, report it with exact details instead of changing app.js. Read both files first, and read the "Page" section of `/root/bench-runs/h4-daaee26c/.team/notes/spec.md` (the spec; every line there needs a test that a plausible wrong implementation would fail). Run `node --test test/app.test.mjs` from the repo root until it passes. No skills needed. Project rules: small focused functions (<50 lines), no console.log, no mutation-heavy cleverness, file may be long (tests) but keep helpers clear; split into `test/helpers/fake-dom.mjs` if the test file would exceed ~800 lines (that's allowed). Do not touch any other file (server.mjs etc. belong to another section). ## Harness design - Load app.js source with fs.readFileSync (path via import.meta.url → ../public/app.js). Run it with `vm.runInContext(source, context)` where context = vm.createContext({ document, fetch }) — ONLY those two globals (plus JS builtins vm provides). This proves app.js uses no other browser global. - Fake DOM: class FakeNode (text node: {nodeType:3, textContent}) and FakeElement {tagName (lowercase), id, children (array of nodes), textContent getter (concat of children text)/setter (replaces children with one text node, or none for ''), value, type, disabled=false, append(...items) (strings become text nodes; elements appended), replaceChildren(...items), addEventListener(type, fn), and a test-only `dispatch(type, event?)` that calls listeners with an event object having `preventDefault()` that records `defaultPrevented=true`}. Do NOT give elements innerHTML, setAttribute, querySelector, etc. — make any access to unknown members detectable: wrap each element in a Proxy whose get trap throws for property names not in the allowed set (allowed: textContent, value, type, disabled, append, replaceChildren, addEventListener, plus test-only internals you prefix with `_` or the harness's own helpers; also allow symbol keys and 'then' returning undefined). Similarly `document` exposes only getElementById and createElement (Proxy that throws on other keys). The reply object passed by fake fetch exposes only `status` and `json` (Proxy throwing on others, e.g. `ok`, `text`). - Build the page's elements by id: booking-form (form), room (select), title, date, start, end (input), book (button), filter-date (input), show-all (button), booking-list (ul), error (p). getElementById returns them; returns null for unknown ids. - Fake fetch: records every call {url, options} in an array and returns a deferred promise. Helpers: `respond(call, status, body)` resolves with reply whose json() returns a deferred/immediate promise of body; `respondJsonFails(call, status)` json() rejects; `fail(call)` rejects fetch with TypeError; `respondDeferredJson(call,status)` returns a handle to resolve json later. Track json() call counts per reply (to assert 204 never calls json()). Use `await flush()` = several `await new Promise(r => setImmediate(r))` to let microtasks run. - Helper to read a list: map each li to its children: text node text and button (tag, type, textContent). ## Tests (each a separate `test()`; be precise) Load: 1. At load, exactly two fetches start synchronously (before any await): first `/api/rooms`, then `/api/bookings` — list fetch starts without waiting for rooms reply. Method GET or absent; no body. 2. Rooms 200 {rooms:['Aurora','Borealis','Cosmos']} → #room has 3 option children in order, each tag 'option', value and textContent equal to name. 3. Rooms error status 500 {error:'boom'} → #error 'boom', #room empty. Error status with body {error: 5} or [ ] or 'str' → 'Request failed.'. Rooms 200 with json() rejecting → 'Could not reach the server.' and room empty. fetch rejects → 'Could not reach the server.'. 4. List 200 {bookings:[{id:1,room:'Aurora',title:'Standup',date:'2026-11-03',start:'09:00',end:'10:00'}]} → one li with exactly 2 children: text node '2026-11-03 09:00-10:00 Aurora: Standup' and button type 'button' text 'Cancel'. Order of multiple bookings preserved exactly as reply (give unsorted order). 5. Empty bookings → single li whose only child is text node 'No bookings.'. 6. Title 'x' appears literally in the text node (plain text). 7. List error status 400 {error:'date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date'} → #error shows it; list unchanged (render a list first via an earlier successful fetch then trigger a change to make a failing one). No reply → 'Could not reach the server.', list unchanged. Successful list fetch leaves an existing #error text alone (set error first via a failed rooms, then success list → error stays). 8. Overlapping list fetches: start A (load), then change filter → B. Resolve B success, then A success with different data → list shows B. Also: A resolves with error/no-reply after B → #error unchanged and list unchanged. Also A resolves first (before B) with error → #error unchanged (outcome ignored since not last started), then B success. Filter: 9. Set filter-date value '2026-11-03', dispatch 'change' → new fetch url exactly '/api/bookings?date=2026-11-03'. Value passed unchanged: value 'a b&c' → url '/api/bookings?date=a b&c'. Dispatching 'input' → no fetch. With empty value → '/api/bookings'. 10. Show all: set filter value, click show-all → filter value '' and exactly one new fetch '/api/bookings'; spy that no 'change'/'input' listener ran (e.g. a change dispatch counter — simplest: count fetches exactly +1). Booking: 11. Submit: event.defaultPrevented true. Fetch '/api/bookings' with options.method 'POST', options.headers deep-equal exactly {'Content-Type':'application/json'} (only key; if headers is a Headers-like object fail), JSON.parse(body) deep-equal {room,title,date,start,end} from control values, title not trimmed (' hi ' stays) and empty fields sent as '' (script does not validate; invalid fields still sent). Book disabled right after submit (synchronously). 12. Submit while book.disabled → preventDefault still called, no fetch. 13. Second submit during pending POST sends nothing. 14. On 201: title emptied, others keep values, #error emptied (preset it), a new list fetch starts. Book re-enabled BEFORE the list refetch: when the list fetch is invoked, book.disabled must already be false (record book.disabled inside fake fetch at call time). Use deferred json: after fetch resolves but before json resolves, book still disabled; after json resolves, enabled. 15. On 409 {error:'room is already booked from 09:00 to 10:00'} → #error exactly that, title kept, no list fetch, book enabled. Non-JSON-object error body → 'Request failed.'. json rejects on 400 → 'Could not reach the server.'. fetch rejects → 'Could not reach the server.', book enabled, no list fetch. 16. POST answered with 204 → json() never called, #error 'Request failed.'. Cancel: 17. Clicking Cancel for booking id 7 → fetch '/api/bookings/7' method 'DELETE'; button disabled at once; re-enabled when settled. 204 → json() not called, #error emptied, list refetched. 404 {error:'booking not found'} → #error 'booking not found' and list refetched. Fetch reject → 'Could not reach the server.' and no refetch, button re-enabled. 404 with json reject → unreachable, no refetch. 18. Cancel click while that button is disabled (pending) → no second DELETE. Static HTML checks (regex/string parsing on index.html): 19. text and the only <h1> text both 'Room bookings' (exactly one h1). 20. form id booking-form has novalidate; inside the form (between its open and close tags): select#room name=room, input type=text id=title name=title, input type=date id=date name=date, input type=time id=start name=start, input type=time id=end name=end, button type=submit id=book text 'Book'. 21. Each label for=<id> with exact text (Room, Title, Date, Start, End, Show date) and the label does not contain its field (label inner content has no tags / no <input|<select). 22. Outside the form: input type=date id=filter-date, button type=button id=show-all text 'Show all', ul#booking-list, p#error role=alert with empty content. 23. No <option, none of 'Aurora','Borealis','Cosmos' in html. No 'http://' or 'https://' in html or app.js. No inline <script> (every script tag has src), no ` on\w+=` attributes. 24. Script element: exactly one <script>, src exactly '/app.js', no type/defer/async attributes, and it is the last element in body (nothing but whitespace between </script> and </body>). Static app.js scan: 25. No import/export statements; none of: innerHTML, outerHTML, insertAdjacentHTML, createTextNode, querySelector, setAttribute, URLSearchParams, encodeURIComponent, window., addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded' / 'load', XMLHttpRequest, .ok, .text(, localStorage, console. I wrote the test file and the fake-DOM helper, and `node --test test/app.test.mjs` passes: 48 tests, 0 failures. I did not edit `public/app.js` or `public/index.html`.

Neither file disagrees with the spec's Page section, as far as the tests cover it.

- **Harness:**
  - `vm.createContext` gets only `document` and `fetch`.
  - Elements, `document`, the fetch reply and the event are Proxies that throw on any member outside the allowed set. Writes to elements are restricted to `textContent`, `value`, `type` and `disabled`.
- **Test-only names:** I called the test-only dispatch helper `_dispatch` rather than `dispatch`, to follow your underscore rule for internals.
- **Prototype caveat:** objects created inside the vm context (such as the fetch `options`) have a different prototype from the test's. So I compare them through `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(...))` or `Object.keys` rather than direct `deepEqual`.
- **Extra cases I added** beyond your list:
  - a list GET answered with 201 counts as an error;
  - a POST answered with 200 counts as an error;
  - a DELETE answered with 200 counts as an error and still refetches;
  - rooms answered with 201 counts as an error;
  - an empty bookings reply replaces earlier items.

I did not run a mutation check against deliberately wrong implementations.
